rationale.conceptual: The method (stress-modified fracture strain) is an established but non-trivial concept requiring understanding of ductile fracture, stress triaxiality, and elastic-plastic FE analysis. Implementing it from the paper's equations and integrating FE results with experimental data for parameter fitting demands careful translation of mechanics concepts into code, beyond a simple off-the-shelf application.
rationale.execution: The pipeline comprises seven distinct computational stages: five axisymmetric tensile bar FE simulations, data extraction and averaging, two exponential regressions, and two 3D pipe FE simulations with subsequent burst-pressure prediction. Each requires FE model setup, large-strain options, and multi-step post-processing. Orchestrating open-source FE tools (e.g., CalculiX) and managing input/output handoffs makes the execution complex and fragile.

The pipeline is multi-stage (5 tensile bar models + 2 pipe models, post-processing, fitting) with careful orchestration of FE tooling.
